metadata.Description: This course introduces essential concepts and methodologies for CMOS analog integrated circuit design, geared toward electronics engineering students with backgrounds in mathematics, physics, circuit theory, electronics, and signal processing. Emphasizing the integration of analytical and simulation approaches, the course utilizes SPICE simulations to illustrate and verify theoretical concepts, providing a practical approach to accurate circuit design.Key topics include MOS transistor modeling, basic gain stages, multi-stage amplifiers, and feedback theory, all foundational to understanding and designing CMOS circuits. The course also covers two-stage operational amplifiers and biasing circuits, with stability and feedback considerations for practical applications. It concludes with a summary of the essential equations and principles, offering students a comprehensive reference for CMOS analog design.

sections.heading: Syllabus Details
rows: Analog Circuit Design_Thiết kế vi mạch tương tự
Social Constructivism, Inquiry-Based Learning, In-class lecture, Active Learning
Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study

This course introduces essential concepts and methodologies for CMOS analog integrated circuit design, geared toward electronics engineering students with backgrounds in mathematics, physics, circuit theory, electronics, and signal processing. Emphasizing the integration of analytical and simulation approaches, the course utilizes SPICE simulations to illustrate and verify theoretical concepts, providing a practical approach to accurate circuit design.Key topics include MOS transistor modeling, basic gain stages, multi-stage amplifiers, and feedback theory, all foundational to understanding and designing CMOS circuits. The course also covers two-stage operational amplifiers and biasing circuits, with stability and feedback considerations for practical applications. It concludes with a summary of the essential equations and principles, offering students a comprehensive reference for CMOS analog design.

- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

rows: Tony Chan Carusone; David A. Johns; Kenneth W. Martin

richRows.text: Tony Chan Carusone; David A. Johns; Kenneth W. Martin

sections.heading: 9 LO(s)
rows: Analyze CMOS analog circuits using mathematical models and simulations.
Apply MOS transistor models in circuit calculations and simulations.
Design and evaluate basic gain stages and small-signal models.
Apply feedback theory to improve amplifier performance and stability.
Design and analyze two-stage opamps with stability considerations.
Design biasing circuits for amplifier operation.
Choose an engineering approach to solving problems, starting from the acquired knowledge essential for the design of electronic circuits.
Demonstrate professional ethics, social responsibility, and environmental impacts into electronic component selection, design, and use throughout the entire product life cycle.
